docs.title: Template::HAML
docs.text:
The latest version of this documentation lives at https://gdonald.github.io/Template-HAML/.

The homepage for Template::HAML is https://github.com/gdonald/Template-HAML.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Template::HAML is an HTML Abstraction Markup Language (HAML) implementation for Raku, built on Raku Grammars. HAML lets you write HTML as an indentation-driven outline rather than as a sea of opening and closing tags.

Currently developed against Raku v6.d.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
example.haml

%html
  %head
    %title Page Title
  %body
    %section.container
      %h1 Title
      %h2 Subtitle
      %p Content
      %ul
        %li Foo
        %li Bar

use Template::HAML;

my $html = HAML.render(:src(slurp 'example.haml'));
say $html;

Output:

<html>
  <head>
    <title>Page Title</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <section class='container'>
      <h1>Title</h1>
      <h2>Subtitle</h2>
      <p>Content</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Foo</li>
        <li>Bar</li>
      </ul>
    </section>
  </body>
</html>

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Template::HAML can be installed using the zef module installation tool:

zef install Template::HAML

docs.title: API
docs.text: The public surface of Template::HAML is small today.

docs.title: HAML.render
docs.text:
use Template::HAML;

my Str $html = HAML.render(:src("..."));
Parameter Type Description :src Str:D The HAML source to parse and render.

Returns the rendered HTML as a Str.

HAML is exported as a class from the Template::HAML module. There is no instance state today; HAML.render is effectively a class method.

docs.title: Internal modules
docs.text:
The implementation is split across several modules under lib/Template/HAML/. These are not part of the stable public API yet, but documented here for contributors:

Module Responsibility Template::HAML::Grammar The Raku Grammar that recognizes HAML source. Template::HAML::Actions Builds the parse tree from grammar matches. Template::HAML::Node Generic tree node holding a Tag or Statement payload. Template::HAML::Tag AST node representing a single HAML tag. Template::HAML::Statement AST node representing a control-flow statement. Template::HAML::Renderer Walks the parse tree and emits HTML. Template::HAML::X Exception types raised by the parser.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: Exception When X::IllegalIndent A line's leading whitespace isn't a valid indent. X::DuplicateId A tag has both #id shorthand and an id: attr.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
A typical project that uses Template::HAML keeps its templates under an app/views/ (or any other) directory, organized by controller / feature, with the .html.haml extension:

my-project/
├── lib/
│   └── MyApp.rakumod
└── app/
    └── views/
        ├── home/
        │   └── index.html.haml
        └── layouts/
            └── app.html.haml

docs.title: Your first template
docs.text:
Create hello.haml:

%html
  %body
    %h1 Hello, world
    %p.lead This page was rendered by Template::HAML.

Render it from Raku:

use Template::HAML;

my $html = HAML.render(:src(slurp 'hello.haml'));
say $html;

You should see:

<html>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, world</h1>
    <p class='lead'>This page was rendered by Template::HAML.</p>
  </body>
</html>

docs.title: Rendering from a string
docs.text:
HAML.render takes any string, so you can also embed templates inline:

my $src = q:to/HAML/;
%section.container
  %h1 Title
  %h2 Subtitle
HAML

say HAML.render(:$src);

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: The test suite lives under t/. Each file uses Raku's built-in Test module.

docs.title: Run the suite
docs.text:
prove6 -Ilib t/

prove6 is a TAP runner; -Ilib puts the project's modules on the include path. Install test-depends from META6.json first if you don't have them:

zef install --deps-only --/test --test-depends .

docs.title: META validation
docs.text: t/000-meta.t6 validates META6.json via Test::META. It runs as part of the suite; if the metadata file is malformed, missing a required field, or refers to a non-existent module, the test fails.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Every push to main and every PR runs prove6 -Ilib t/ on Linux via the GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Template::HAML supports a Ruby-style attribute hash on any tag:

%a{href: '/about', title: 'About us'} About

<a href='/about' title='About us'>About</a>

docs.title: Value types
docs.text:
Today the supported value types inside { ... } are:

  • Single-quoted strings: 'value'
  • Double-quoted strings: "value"
  • Symbols (treated as strings): :value
%input{type: :text, name: 'email'}
%a{href: "/", class: 'home'} Home

docs.title: Multiple attributes
docs.text:
Separate attributes with commas:

%a{href: '/', class: 'home', id: 'home-link'} Home

<a href='/' class='home' id='home-link'>Home</a>

docs.title: Class shorthand merges with class:
docs.text:
The .classname shorthand on a tag merges with any class: entry in the attribute hash. The two forms compose:

%p.lead{class: 'intro'} Welcome

<p class='lead intro'>Welcome</p>

docs.title: Indentation
docs.text: HAML uses indentation to express nesting. A line that's indented further than the previous line becomes a child of that line; a line at the same indent is a sibling; a line at a shallower indent closes one or more parents.

docs.title: Two-space indent
docs.text:
Template::HAML currently expects two-space indentation:

%section.container
  %h1 Title
  %ul
    %li Foo
    %li Bar

<section class='container'>
  <h1>Title</h1>
  <ul>
    <li>Foo</li>
    <li>Bar</li>
  </ul>
</section>

docs.title: Inconsistent indentation is rejected
docs.text:
An odd-spaced indent is rejected with X::IllegalIndent:

%section
   %h1 Title

Illegal indentation

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
A tag in HAML is introduced by a sigil at the start of a line:

Sigil Meaning % Element name (%p, %div, %h1) . Class on a <div> (.container) # Id on a <div> (#main)

docs.title: Element names
docs.text:
%p Hello
%div A block
%h1 Title

renders to:

<p>Hello</p>
<div>A block</div>
<h1>Title</h1>

docs.title: Class shorthand
docs.text:
%tag.classname adds a class to an element:

%p.lead Welcome

<p class='lead'>Welcome</p>

You can chain multiple classes:

%p.lead.intro Welcome

<p class='lead intro'>Welcome</p>

docs.title: Id shorthand
docs.text:
%tag#name sets the element's id:

%section#main

<section id='main'></section>

docs.title: Combining shorthand and attributes
docs.text:
The class shorthand merges with a class: attribute hash entry:

%p.lead{class: 'intro'} Welcome

<p class='lead intro'>Welcome</p>

See Attributes for the full attribute hash syntax.
